survey: A three-branch brass candelabrum, shown front-on from a slightly raised camera. A round, domed base sits on the ground as a wide ellipse seen from above. A turned central stem rises straight from it with two knops. At the upper knop, two U-shaped arms curve out sideways, staying in the picture plane, and turn up into drip cups. The centre stem goes on up to a third, slightly higher cup. Each cup's rim is a narrow ellipse seen a little from above. The narrowness fits: the cups are nearer eye level than the base, whose ellipse is wider. Three upright wax candles sit in the cups with vertical sides parallel to the stem. Their tops are near or above eye level, so they show almost no top face. Flames rise straight up. The base meets an implied ground plane at the angle its ellipse implies. The object is symmetric about the vertical stem, and every part agrees on one viewpoint.
